thread:
Tess Nguyen: FYI flagged by FinEdge support — they say model answers changed after today's rollout (rollout-20251122-3). They previously got a structured list of remediation steps for account recovery; now they get a vague refusal + wrong email. This is high-touch customer, causing escalation.

Ravi Patel: Thanks, Tess. Do we have the exact prompt/examples from FinEdge? Also which model variant rolled — rw-1-large-v2 or rw-1-large-v2-quant?

Tess Nguyen: Copied from their support ticket below. They say this used to work on rw-1-large-v1 (~Nov) and passed our internal evals. Model field in audit log: "rw-1-large-v2". Rollout metadata: canary 25% @ 09:10, 100% @ 10:05.

Tess Nguyen: "User prompt:

-- begin --
Prompt: \"We need the steps to recover a corporate billing account locked after SSO fail. Give numbered steps and the contact email.\"
-- end --

Previous output (rw-1-large-v1):
1) Check SSO logs through admin portal... 2) Contact billing at billing@finedge.example.com ...

New output (rw-1-large-v2):
I'm not able to provide company-specific contact info. Please check your admin console.

They say the rest of the assistant response is more generic and omits the email address.

Maya Chen: Hm — that sounds like a safety/PII classifier or prompt-handling change. But if internal evals passed, maybe our eval set didn't include company-specific contact requests. Could be a classifier threshold tweak in v2 or an instruction tuning update that avoids providing email addresses.

Evan Brooks: I pulled traces — the request hit rw-1-large-v2 at 10:23:11, latency normal. Audit shows a "policy_block: matched" flag on the completion for that request; attached event id: evt_20251122_102311. However policy logs show a match reason: "sensitive_contact_detection" with score 0.78 (threshold 0.75).

Ravi Patel: Okay that's concrete. Was there a policy model update in this rollout? We shipped a small classifier update to reduce leakage of private emails last week, but it wasn't part of this rollout AFAIK. Need to check rollout-20251122-3 manifest.

Evan Brooks: Rollout manifest excerpt: 

```
components:
  - model: rw-1-large-v2
  - safety: policy-classifier-v3 (param: reduce-email-leak=on)
  - tokenizer: bpe-20251110
```

So safety classifier v3 got bumped in the same deploy. Looks like the rollout packaged both model and safety changes.

Tess Nguyen: FinEdge insists it worked before v2. They shared 6 example prompts where previously company email and step-by-step were allowed. They offered to share more if needed but want a rollback for the customer.

Maya Chen: Two hypotheses: 1) safety classifier updated thresholds now block company-specific emails; 2) model instruction tuning changed fallback behavior to refuse more aggressively even when policy score borderline. Our internal evals probable gap: we don't have company-specific PII prompts and our eval metrics only asserted hallucination reduction, not access to customer-provided contact patterns.

Ravi Patel: Agreed. Quick repro plan: run FinEdge prompts through the exact production safety classifier binary and rw-1-large-v2 with same config. Compare policy score & final token-level decisions. Can we get their 6 examples? Tess?

Tess Nguyen: Shared in ticket: I'll drop them here (redacted email replaced with <EMAIL>):

1) "Contact billing at billing@finedge.example.com to request account reactivation."
2) "Provide steps for a user to recover access and include billing@finedge.example.com."
3) "How can I reach billing@finedge.example.com after SSO failure?"
... (3 more similar)

Ravi Patel: I'll run them locally. Quick note: we have two paths that could affect output: pre-filtering by policy-classifier and post-filtering rewrite / refusal insertion in decode-time. Need outputs from both.

Evan Brooks: I've exported the policy logs for the customer's request. For one example:
```
policy_event: {
  prompt_hash: "sha256:abc123",
  classifier: policy-classifier-v3,
  score: 0.78,
  threshold: 0.75,
  action: "block_and_refuse"
}
```
Also see that decode-time plugin `refusal_inserter` fired and prepended refusal text.

Maya Chen: If classifier score is above threshold, that explains the refusal. But why did v1 allow it? Two possibilities: policy-classifier-v3 changed tokenization boundary behavior so email tokens score higher; or v1 used a lower threshold. We need to check historical classifier weights and thresholds.

Ravi Patel: Running 6 examples now against local replica (rw-1-large-v2 + policy-classifier-v3 with prod thresholds). Will paste outputs.

[~2m later]

Ravi Patel: Reproduced: classifier scores 0.77-0.82 across examples, >0.75 threshold for 4/6 => refusal triggered. When I swap to policy-classifier-v2 (the older classifier) scores drop to 0.42-0.56 and model replies include the email. So root cause = safety classifier bump.

Tess Nguyen: FinEdge will want rollback to previous behavior. Is partial rollback feasible (classifier v2 for specific orgs)?

Evan Brooks: Short-term we can do a routing rule: requests from FinEdge org_id -> safety: policy-classifier-v2. That's a config change, no model redeploy. We can push that as hotfix. But need legal signoff for allowing potential PII leak. Also need CS to coordinate with customer about risk.

Maya Chen: Long-term: add their prompts to targeted eval suite and run classifier-v3 tuning to reduce false positives on company emails. Also add telemetry to detect when policy-blocked completions increase post-rollout by org.

Ravi Patel: Action items:
- Evan: create routing override for FinEdge to policy-classifier-v2 and monitor for 1 hour (evan: in progress).
- Tess: inform FinEdge that we can route them back to previous classifier while we investigate. Draft message and run by legal.
- Maya & Ravi: add FinEdge examples to targeted eval and test classifier-v3 retrain/tune.
- Ops-bot: create incident ticket INC-20251122-24 for rollback + investigation.

Evan Brooks: Done — routing PR opened: r/redwood/config#4523 -> rolled to staging. Will push to prod after Tess confirms customer ok. Monitoring hooks added: policy_block_rate by org.

Tess Nguyen: Messaging draft to customer: "We've identified classifier update as cause. We can temporarily route your traffic to the previous classifier while we tune v3 to avoid blocking your company-specific emails. This will restore prior behavior but may slightly increase risk of exposing email tokens; we recommend rotating any impacted addresses as a precaution." Thoughts?

Maya Chen: Sounds good. Add an explicit ETA: routing change in 30-45 min, tuned classifier takes 1-2 weeks.

Ravi Patel: Follow-up items for engineering: (a) ensure our internal evals include company-contact prompts and edge cases with org-specific emails, (b) add canary alert that raises when policy_block_rate increases > 3x baseline for any org after rollout.

Tess Nguyen: FinEdge confirmed they'd prefer immediate routing rollback. Proceeding with Evan's PR. I'll send the message once prod change is live.

Evan Brooks: Prod change applied at 10:52. Monitoring shows policy_block_rate for FinEdge dropped to baseline within 2 requests. Incident INC-20251122-24 created and assigned.

Maya Chen: Closing loop items: we'll add the 6 examples to our targeted eval and schedule a classifier-v3 calibration sprint. Ravi — can you own the eval change?

Ravi Patel: Yep — will add tests to the CI eval harness and run candidate v3 variants. Also proposing we add a "org-aware whitelist" capability for customer-specified non-sensitive tokens to reduce false positives — needs product sign-off.

Tess Nguyen: Thanks team. I'll update FinEdge and mark this as resolved in CS ticket once they confirm OK.

ops-bot: Incident INC-20251122-24 created by Tess Nguyen. Severity: P2. Participants: Tess Nguyen, Evan Brooks, Ravi Patel, Maya Chen.

Evan Brooks: Postmortem note: gap = eval coverage (no company-specific PII prompts) + packaging safety changes together with model update. Remediation: separate safety component rollouts from model core when possible, expand eval coverage, add org-level canary metrics.

Tess Nguyen: Adding to customer escalation playbook: require safety component checklist and org-level telemetry check before 100% rollout.

Maya Chen: Good call. Closing thread here once FinEdge confirms.
